Zero-inflated continuous parameter binomial regression

Source: R/zi.R
zi_cpb.Rd

Fits the zero-inflated CPB. The model mixes a structural-zero process (a logistic model for the probability pi that a unit is a structural zero) with an untruncated CPB for the count, so a zero can arise either structurally or as a sampling zero from the CPB. Unlike hurdle_cpb(), the likelihood does not factorize, so the parameters are estimated by direct joint maximum likelihood. The mixture likelihood's optima differ with the structural share of zeros, so the search starts from points that span it: separate fits (a zero-truncated CPB on the positives and a logit of the zero indicator), the zero-inflated Poisson's coefficients, and a low-inflation start (a constant structural-zero probability of 0.02), followed by a BFGS pass; it is cross-checked against an expectation-maximization climb of the same observed-data likelihood, keeping the better optimum. The separation check (Separation) restarts the final polish from any better point it finds. An EM-only path (method = "em") is retained for comparison.

Usage

zi_cpb(
  formula,
  data,
  zero = NULL,
  fe = NULL,
  zero_fe = NULL,
  method = c("ml", "em"),
  se = c("none", "bootstrap"),
  B = 500,
  cluster = NULL,
  max.support = NULL,
  maxit = 200,
  tol = 1e-06,
  offset = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  cores = 1L,
  support = c("ceiling", "floor")
)

Arguments

formula

Intensity (count) model formula (y ~ x).

data

A data frame.

zero

Optional one-sided formula (~ z) for the zero-inflation model; defaults to the intensity model's right-hand side.

fe

Optional column name for unit fixed effects in the intensity (count) component. Under method = "ml" the unit effects enter as plug-in offsets from a first-stage fit to the positive counts, and on King's support the fit is then polished on the observed-data likelihood with every unit's effect free, so that it is a joint maximum of the mixture likelihood (on the floor support the fit keeps the plug-in effects, which are not a joint maximum: a unit whose positive counts are all 1 takes an arbitrary point of the first stage's flat set, so the inflation equation and the log-likelihood can depend on the order of the rows); under method = "em" a classification (hard-assignment) step handles the structural zeros before the same polish. A unit with no positive count is left out of the estimation, as fixest leaves such units out of a Poisson fixed-effects fit: at the maximum its count effect is minus infinity, so its zeros are certain whatever its structural-zero probability, and its rows add nothing to the likelihood or the degrees of freedom. Its rows stay in the fit at that limit (the effect at the cpb_fe() sentinel, 30 log units below the unit's largest linear predictor), with fitted means of zero, and the fit records the units in zero_units and their number in n_zero_units. Their structural-zero probability is NA where the zero equation would give them their own dummy (zero_fe), which their zeros cannot identify. On the floor support such units stay in the estimation with a filled-in count effect (the smallest estimated effect minus 2 under "ml", the mean effect under "em").

zero_fe

Optional column name for fixed effects in the zero-inflation equation, entered as factor dummies (opt-in). On King's support the dummy of a unit with no positive count is not counted in the degrees of freedom (see compare_models(), Degrees of freedom), and in new data such a unit's rows get the structural-zero probability one and those of a unit whose every count is positive (zero_fe_one_units) zero; a unit the fit has not seen, or every row when newdata lacks the column, enters at the zero equation's reference unit.

method

Estimation method: "ml" (default) is direct joint maximum likelihood from the starts described above; "em" is expectation-maximization, retained for comparison but prone to a degenerate structural-zero-probability collapse under heavy zero-inflation.

se

Coefficient inference: "none" (default) or "bootstrap".

B

Bootstrap resamples when se = "bootstrap".

cluster

Optional cluster for the bootstrap (a column name or vector); under fixed effects the units are resampled by default. The mixture EM makes the bootstrap costly, so keep B modest.

max.support

Guard on the evaluated support of the count component; see cpb(). The default NULL sets max(500, 10 * max(y)) (500 on the floor support). It is kept with the fit for simulate().

maxit

Optimizer iteration budget (scaled internally for the joint maximization; also the EM iteration cap under method = "em").

tol

Relative convergence tolerance on the observed-data log-likelihood.

offset

Optional exposure offset (log scale) for the count component: a numeric vector or the name of a column in data, making the count a rate model. Supported for method = "ml" without fe; with fe, an offset is refused with an error. The bootstrap carries the offset through every replicate.

weights

Optional frequency weights (a numeric vector or a column name); see cpb(). Supported for method = "ml".

cores

Worker processes for the bootstrap; see cpb().

support

The CPB's support, "ceiling" (King's CPB, the default) or "floor"; see cpb().

Value

An object of class "zi_cpb". Its component separation holds the separation check (see Separation).

Details

The inflation equation uses a logit link. For a probit or cloglog inflation link, use zi_count() (Poisson/NB/COM-Poisson count), whose link argument covers the binary stage.

Separation

A zero contributes log(pi + (1 - pi) f0) to the likelihood, which rises with pi, and a positive count contributes log(1 - pi) + log f(y), which falls with it. So a coefficient of the zero-inflation equation can grow without bound, and the likelihood with it, under three conditions. The zeros it pushes toward pi = 1 can go there freely, and so can the positives it pushes toward pi = 0. The count component's probability of a zero, f0, covers the zeros it pushes toward pi = 0. Unlike separation in a logistic regression, this needs no covariate that splits the zeros from the positives. So a hurdle_cpb() whose participation logit uses the same covariates can have a finite maximum while the mixture has none. The optimizer then stops somewhere along the divergent path. The zero equation's coefficients there are not estimates, and the log-likelihood approximates a supremum, so likelihood comparisons with the fit (likelihood ratio, AIC, Vuong) lack their usual reference distributions.

After the fit, the profile likelihood of each covariate coefficient in the zero equation is evaluated at the estimate. It is evaluated again at 10 and at 100 standard deviations of its covariate further from zero. Each time, the other zero-equation coefficients are re-maximized with the count component held at its estimate. The fit warns when a coefficient's profile 100 standard deviations out is less than qchisq(0.95, 1) / 2 below its value at the estimate. That coefficient's 95% profile interval then reaches past an effect of 100 on the log-odds per standard deviation, and the data put no useful bound on it. This covers a coefficient with no finite estimate and one whose finite maximum lies on a near-flat ridge, which a fit cannot tell apart. Holding the count component fixed can only lower the profile, so the full model's interval is at least as wide. Every profile can also reach the no-inflation boundary, where each structural-zero probability is zero and the zero equation drops out. A coefficient whose profile at the estimate lies within qchisq(0.95, 1) / 2 of that limit is unbounded because the data show little inflation, not by separation, so it is not flagged, and the fit is reported as near the boundary instead (zi_test() tests it). The intercept and the zero_fe dummies are not checked. Their limits are the no-inflation boundary (zi_test()) and the boundaries of single units (a unit with no positive count, whose structural-zero probability goes to one, as in a fixed-effects logit; with fe, such a unit is left out of the estimation, see fe). The component separation of the fit holds:

  • diverging: the terms the data do not bound;

  • profile: the profile steps;

  • short_of_max: how far the best point the check found lies above the fit, with the count component unchanged. That point can come from the re-maximization at the estimate, when the fit is not a stationary point of the zero equation, or from a profile that rises above its value at the estimate, since the mixture likelihood is not concave and a profile can rise before it falls. A positive value means the optimizer stopped at least that far below the maximum;

  • best: the zero-equation coefficients at that point (NULL when there is none);

  • restarts, restart_gain: when the check finds a point at least 0.01 higher, the fit restarts its final polish there, with every parameter it estimates free, keeps the result only if it gains, and checks again, up to three times. These record the restarts kept and their total gain in log-likelihood. The other components describe the final fit;

  • no_inflation, inflation_gain: whether the best point lies within qchisq(0.95, 1) / 2 of the no-inflation limit (the count component held), and its distance from it;

  • n_extreme: the number of observations whose structural-zero probability is numerically 0 or 1, outside units that lie wholly at one edge.

zi_gec() and zi_count() run the same check.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
n <- 800; x <- rnorm(n); z <- rnorm(n)
y <- rzicpb(n, lambda = exp(1.3 + 0.5 * x), alpha = 0.5, pi = plogis(-0.5 + 0.8 * z))
zi_cpb(y ~ x, data = data.frame(y = y, x = x, z = z), zero = ~ z)
#> Zero-Inflated Continuous Parameter Binomial
#> Call:  zi_cpb(formula = y ~ x, data = data.frame(y = y, x = x, z = z),     zero = ~z)
#> N: 800   optimizer iterations: 35   logLik: -1264.1
#> 
#> Intensity (CPB) coefficients:
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>      1.2940      0.5137 
#> Intensity alpha (shape): 0.5124 
#> 
#> Zero-inflation (logit link) -- positive coefficients raise P(structural zero), i.e. lower the
#> chance of a positive count (the opposite direction from a hurdle participation model):
#> (Intercept)           z 
#>     -0.3891      0.7048 
#> Mean structural-zero probability: 0.413 
# }
